evals.prompt: Use the estimation skill. Estimate these 5 backlog items for TaskFlow using Fibonacci, compare each to our 3-point reference story 'Login with email': (1) Add CAPTCHA to signup, (2) Migrate the entire checkout flow to Stripe Elements, (3) Fix typo in footer, (4) Build admin export-to-CSV with filters, (5) Research: should we use Pusher or Ably for realtime? Say which items need splitting or a different treatment, and why. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Per-item estimate with Fibonacci value, rationale comparing to the 3-point reference, complexity factors named. Item (2) flagged for decomposition (>8). Item (5) suggested as a spike with timebox.
expectations: The answer checks the project's estimate system with project_estimate(action=retrieve, project_id=...)
The answer writes the agreed value with workitem(action=update, ..., point=<n>)
The answer rates the footer typo (item 3) at 1 point
The answer says the Stripe Elements migration (item 2) is more than 8 points and sends it to the task-decomposition skill
The answer treats the Pusher or Ably question (item 5) as a timeboxed spike
The answer uses only the values 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 13

evals.prompt: Use the estimation skill. Estimate this story: 'As a user I can reset my password via email link. Must work on mobile. Must rate-limit to prevent abuse. Must handle expired/already-used links gracefully.' Compare against our reference story 'Login with email' = 3 points. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: Suggests 5 or 8 points with rationale referencing multiple components (FE + API + email service + security), compared to the reference.
expectations: The answer uses the 'Password reset flow' reference pattern from the skill (5-8 pts)
The answer explicitly compares to the 3-point reference story
The answer names the complexity factors: email service, rate limiting, expiry handling, mobile
The answer flags the security-critical aspect as a risk that justifies the higher end

evals.prompt: Use the estimation skill. Planning poker for 'Migrate auth middleware': Alice voted 3, Bob voted 5, Carol voted 13. How do I handle this? In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Identifies divergent spread (>2 Fibonacci numbers), asks highest and lowest to explain, suggests re-vote after discussion, or split the item if Carol's concerns are structural.
expectations: The answer detects that spread 3→13 is too divergent to just average
The answer asks Carol (highest) and Alice (lowest) to explain reasoning first
The answer recommends re-vote after discussion, not averaging
The answer flags that if the gap stays wide, the item should be split via task-decomposition skill

evals.prompt: Use the estimation skill. Our team is new and has no reference stories yet. When should we use t-shirt sizes and when Fibonacci for our first sprints, how do the two convert, what do we set up after the first sprint, and what do we avoid when estimating?
evals.expected_output: Recommends t-shirt sizing for initial backlog triage, Fibonacci once references are established.
expectations: The answer says t-shirt sizing suits roadmap planning, initial backlog triage and quick group sessions, and Fibonacci suits sprint planning, velocity tracking and capacity
The answer gives the t-shirt to points conversion (for example M = 3, L = 5, XL = 8)
The answer suggests establishing 1-3 reference stories (a completed, well-understood item such as 'Login with email' = 3) for Fibonacci calibration
The answer warns against estimating in hours (anti-pattern from skill)
